claim.why_it_matters: Wrong heading level. Every other statement clause in Section VI is a level-2 heading (`## 6.20 THE MULTIPLY STATEMENT`, `## 6.21 THE PERFORM STATEMENT`); 6.22 is promoted to level 1, so it sits at the same level as the document's top headings and breaks the outline. The 6.23 SET heading on a later page shows the same promotion.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page VI-122 shows '6.22 THE SEARCH STATEMENT' as the first line inside the boxed general-format frame, typeset like every other statement-clause heading. The markdown has the heading text, so nothing is missing, but it is written '# ║6.22 THE SEARCH STATEMENT║' (line 14483). The 6.20 and 6.21 headings are '## ...' (lines 13988, 14051), and 6.23 SET is also promoted to '# ' (line 14643). The '║' characters are the box's border, picked up by OCR; they are not on the page as text. So the heading-level error is real and breaks the clause outline that section-locating tools depend on. It does not change the standard's normative wording.
verdict.corrected_description: The heading is present but at the wrong level, and its text is wrong too: '# ║6.22 THE SEARCH STATEMENT║' should be '## 6.22 THE SEARCH STATEMENT'. It sits at level 1 where its siblings 6.20 and 6.21 are at level 2, and the '║' characters are OCR artifacts of the boxed frame. The kind is a wrong heading level plus stray glyphs, not a missing heading. 6.23 THE SET STATEMENT (md line 14643) is promoted to level 1 in the same way.
